doc.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999

title: Threats from Texas men and first encounters with Jim Crow
summary: A confrontation outside a Texas club, then restaurants and water fountains in the South.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Did you ever have any problems with the fact that it was an integrated band racially?

I’m sure there was, but I’m trying to think of what it was. In fact you know Ken Burns is doing a thing, right? And they came to my house two or three years ago and they came in with a crew of ten people. My basement is about as big as their — they had things all over the place. And they interviewed me and I told this story about we were in Texas and we were playing in a place called the Seven something, and we had taken a break and I went outside to get some fresh air, it was very hot in the room even though it was air conditioning, you know it gets hot. So I went outside and while I was sitting like this getting some sun, it got dark and I opened my eyes and I saw about four big Texas guys with the big necks like this, and they said, “Hey man.” I said, “Yeah?” “How come you play with a nigger band?” I said, “What?” They said, “You heard me.” I said, “What the hell are you talking about, man?” I said, “You know who that is? That’s Louis Armstrong.” “So what?” I said, “what do you mean, so what? Didn’t you pay to come in to see him?” The guy says, “yeah.” I said, “how much did you pay?” I forget, ten dollars?

I said, “I’m getting paid to work with him, you’re a bigger jerk than I am, aren’t you?” And just as I said that, Cozy was coming out to call me or something, and he heard me say that. He says, “Marty, telephone.” So he came to grab me and he pulled me in. He says, “are you crazy?” I said, “what?” He says, “didn’t you see the size of those guys?” I said, “yeah but did you hear what they said, I mean, come on, Cozy.” And the only other thing I saw was a couple of incidences. One was we were down south some place, well three or four. Now I had never worked with a mixed band before, so it was white bands. And in fact when I joined Louis it was three and three. Three white guys, three black guys, and a girl. And we were doing a one-nighter someplace, I forget, Texas or someplace down south. And I had never played the south before, strangely enough, with all the bands I’d been with. Now here I am with a mixed band and we were down south right? So we walked into a, it was about 7:00 in the morning and we stopped for breakfast at a restaurant. And we walked in and there was two or three guys behind the counter and they disappeared into the kitchen. So we sat down and Frenchie was the manager, he says, “all right guys let’s leave.” I said, “wait a minute, we just came in.” I was so naive, I didn’t know. He said, “let’s leave.” I said, “where we going? We didn’t eat.” He says, “Marty, let’s leave.” I said to somebody, “what the hell happened?” No, come on, Marty, did you see the guys disappear? I said oh yeah, the guys behind the counter, when we walked in they walked — so that was my first inkling what was happening. Then we stopped at a place, a gas station, it had rest rooms. And we went to the rest rooms and it said “Blacks” and “Whites.” And there was like a water fountain. So I went to get some water, and Velma came and I said, “Velma, the water is so cold, it’s delicious.” She said, “you know I can’t drink that.” I said, “get outta here. You come over here.” Velma was about 300 pounds and I was this skinny when I joined him. And I said, “go ahead, I’ll cover you.” She said, “get outta here, you jerk.” I said, “don’t worry Velma, I’ve got you covered.” And let me see there was another place. Oh I know one, we were playing in Austin Texas at a ballroom. And this is one thing that really surprised me because we had a guy that used to sell the programs in front of the theater when we were doing concerts. You know, the big programs that they sell with all the pictures and everything. So we’re going by bus and the bus breaks down about 20 or 30 miles outside of town. Okay?
